issue.title: Memoize Locale.create on the resolved configuration

repository.name: luxon
repository.description: ⏱ A library for working with dates and times in JS

issue.body:
Fixes #1802.

## Problem

Every `DateTime` and `Duration` carries a `Locale`, and `Locale.create` returns a fresh instance on every call. A `Locale` allocates its own `weekdaysCache`, `monthsCache`, `meridiemCache`, `eraCache`, `fastNumbersCached` slot and Intl config string: 8 objects and about 480 bytes retained in Node (V8 without pointer compression; Chrome stores roughly half). In a heap snapshot of a large single-page application, 24,807 retained `DateTime`s were accompanied by 24,769 `Locale`s, 13.6 MB retained in total, with the `Locale` accounting for 396 of every 550 bytes; `Locale` was the fifth largest owning class in that heap, even though only a handful of distinct configurations existed.

The per-instance lazy caches also mean that `dt.weekdayLong`, `dt.monthLong`, `Info.months(..., { locale })` and friends rebuild their name lists through `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for every new `DateTime` in a non-English locale, because each one starts with empty caches.

## Fix

A `Locale` is never mutated after construction (every change goes through `clone()`, which builds a new one), and its lazily populated lists are pure functions of its configuration. So `Locale.create` now memoizes on the resolved configuration, the way `IANAZone.create` memoizes zones, and `Locale.resetCache()` (behind `Settings.resetCaches()`) clears it with the other caches.

How the lookup works:

- The key is computed **after** the `Settings` defaults are applied, so `Settings.defaultLocale = "de"` at runtime yields a different entry and a fresh `Locale`; instances created earlier keep formatting in their original language.
- Entries are grouped in one bucket per resolved locale string and matched on the remaining fields directly: `numberingSystem` and `outputCalendar` by identity, `weekSettings` by value (`validateWeekSettings` returns a fresh object per call), and whether the locale was specified. That last bit matters because `clone()` only redefaults Locales that fell back to the system locale or `en-US`, so an explicit `"en-US"` and the `defaultToEN` fallback are not interchangeable. The scans are plain indexed loops rather than `for...of`, so the ES5 builds do not go through the iterator protocol on every creation.
- No composite string key is built. A first version keyed a `Map` on `JSON.stringify` of the five fields and regressed `DateTime.now()` by about 17%; a second version kept a fast path for bare locales but any global `Settings.defaultWeekSettings` / `defaultNumberingSystem` / `defaultOutputCalendar` pushed every creation back onto the slow path (`DateTime.now()` −25%). Building and hashing a fresh key costs more than the allocation it replaces; a `Map` hit on an already-hashed locale string plus a few comparisons does not.
- The cache is bounded to 100 locale strings × 20 entries each, with clear-all eviction. Ordinary applications never reach either limit; they only protect callers that pass unbounded distinct locale strings or `weekSettings` values.

Two consequences of sharing needed handling:

- **Deep freezing.** A deep-freeze that walks own properties (deep-freeze, redux-freeze, NgRx's dev-mode `strictStateImmutability`) freezes `dt.loc` along with the `DateTime`. Before, that only broke the frozen instance (#1104). With sharing it would have broken every other `DateTime` with the same configuration for the rest of the process. `create` now treats a non-extensible cached instance as a miss and replaces it, so the blast radius stays what it was.
- **Cached name lists.** `Info.months` / `monthsFormat` / `weekdays` / `weekdaysFormat` / `meridiems` / `eras` used to return the Intl-derived array of a throwaway `Locale`, so callers could mutate it freely. The Intl branch of `listStuff` now returns a copy of the cached list, as the English branch and `Info.getWeekendWeekdays` already did, so the shared lists stay intact. `DateTime#monthLong` and friends go through the same path; the copy is 2 to 12 elements. The copy is made in `Locale` rather than in `Info` so the English path is not copied twice.

`Locale.equals` was not used as the key because it ignores `weekSettings` and `specifiedLocale`.

## Numbers

Node 26.7.0 on macOS, `src/` build, retained heap for 50,000 `DateTime.fromMillis` values with forced GC before and after:

|                               | before | after |
| ----------------------------- | ------ | ----- |
| bytes retained per `DateTime` | 680    | 208   |
| distinct `Locale` objects     | 50,000 | 1     |

Micro-benchmark (Benchmark.js, one tree per process, three interleaved rounds, medians with the relative margin of error of the median round):

| case | master | this branch | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DateTime.now()` | 5.24M ±0.2% | 5.76M ±0.2% | 1.10x |
| `DateTime.fromMillis` | 5.78M ±0.2% | 6.34M ±0.1% | 1.10x |
| `DateTime.local` with numbers | 1.71M ±0.2% | 1.76M ±0.2% | 1.03x |
| `DateTime.fromISO` | 759K ±0.2% | 772K ±0.2% | 1.02x |
| `DateTime.fromObject` with `locale` | 1.97M ±0.3% | 1.95M ±0.2% | 0.99x |
| `DateTime.fromObject` with `numberingSystem` | 1.87M ±0.2% | 1.93M ±0.2% | 1.03x |
| `DateTime.fromObject` with `weekSettings` | 1.79M ±0.2% | 1.82M ±0.3% | 1.02x |
| `DateTime.fromObject` with a `-u-` locale | 539K ±0.3% | 1.90M ±0.2% | 3.54x |
| `DateTime#setLocale` | 11.08M ±0.5% | 12.67M ±0.3% | 1.14x |
| `DateTime#reconfigure` with `numberingSystem` | 8.42M ±0.2% | 11.78M ±0.3% | 1.40x |
| `DateTime#setLocale` on an `arab` DateTime | 9.55M ±0.2% | 12.37M ±0.6% | 1.30x |
| `DateTime#toFormat` | 2.11M ±0.8% | 2.24M ±0.2% | 1.06x |
| `DateTime#toLocaleString` (control, does not reach `Locale.create`) | 1.44M ±0.2% | 1.44M ±0.2% | 1.00x |
| `DateTime#toLocaleString` with opts | 1.82M ±0.2% | 1.82M ±0.2% | 1.00x |
| `Duration.fromObject` with `locale` | 15.26M ±0.3% | 17.04M ±0.5% | 1.12x |
| fresh `fr` `DateTime#weekdayLong` | 110K ±0.2% | 1.75M ±1.3% | 15.9x |
| `Info.months("long", { locale: "es" })` | 67K ±0.4% | 23.71M ±0.3% | 356x |
| `DateTime.now()` with `Settings.defaultWeekSettings` set | 4.60M ±0.2% | 4.69M ±0.3% | 1.02x |
| `DateTime#setLocale` with `Settings.defaultWeekSettings` set | 9.55M ±0.3% | 10.50M ±0.9% | 1.10x |
| `DateTime.fromMillis` with `Settings.defaultNumberingSystem` set | 4.16M ±0.2% | 4.83M ±0.2% | 1.16x |
| `DateTime.now()` with `Settings.defaultOutputCalendar` set | 4.23M ±1.2% | 4.74M ±0.2% | 1.12x |
| `DateTime.now()` with `Settings.defaultLocale` set | 4.85M ±0.2% | 4.94M ±0.3% | 1.02x |

The two `toLocaleString` rows are the noise floor: they never call `Locale.create`, so they show what a 0% change looks like on this machine. `setLocale` on a bare DateTime moved between +12% and +14% across runs and should be read as "faster, amount uncertain".

Repository suite (`npm run benchmark`, three interleaved rounds per tree, medians; rows whose relative margin of error reached 10% in any round are marked):

| case | master | this branch | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DateTime.now` | 5.26M | 5.72M | 1.09x |
| `DateTime.fromObject` with locale | 2.09M | 2.06M | 0.98x |
| `DateTime.local` with numbers | 1.71M | 1.74M | 1.02x |
| `DateTime.local` with numbers and zone | 311K | 314K | 1.01x |
| `DateTime.fromISO` | 777K | 792K | 1.02x |
| `DateTime.fromSQL` | 869K | 888K | 1.02x |
| `DateTime.fromFormat` | 192K | 193K | 1.01x |
| `DateTime.fromFormat` with zone | 92K | 92K | 1.00x |
| `DateTime.fromFormatParser` | 648K | 663K | 1.02x |
| `DateTime.fromFormatParser` with zone | 147K | 149K | 1.01x |
| `DateTime#setZone` | 373K | 371K | 1.00x |
| `DateTime#toFormat` | 2.05M | 2.11M | 1.03x |
| `DateTime#toFormat` with macro | 1.21M | 1.24M | 1.02x |
| `DateTime#toFormat` with macro no cache | 21K | 19K | 0.95x (RME up to 14%) |
| `DateTime#format` in german | 723K | 753K | 1.04x |
| `DateTime#format` in german and no-cache | 16K | 19K | 1.18x (RME up to 26%) |
| `DateTime#add` | 818K | 855K | 1.04x |
| `DateTime#toISO` | 7.70M | 7.36M | 0.96x |
| `DateTime#toLocaleString` | 1.46M | 1.35M | 0.93x (RME up to 21%) |
| `DateTime#toLocaleString` in utc | 645K | 643K | 1.00x (RME up to 34%) |
| `DateTime#toRelativeCalendar` | 82K | 84K | 1.03x |
| `Info.months` with existing locale | 64.05M | 63.96M | 1.00x |
| `Info.months` | 15.70M | 26.47M | 1.69x |
| `Info.monthsFormat` with existing locale | 63.04M | 63.89M | 1.01x |
| `Info.monthsFormat` | 15.70M | 26.74M | 1.70x |
| `Info.weekdays` with existing locale | 55.73M | 56.71M | 1.02x |
| `Info.weekdays` | 18.92M | 27.25M | 1.44x |
| `Info.weekdaysFormat` with existing locale | 56.44M | 57.14M | 1.01x |
| `Info.weekdaysFormat` | 18.99M | 27.24M | 1.43x |

Nothing outside the noise floor got slower. The rows below 1.00x are `fromObject` with locale at 0.98x, inside the noise floor and 0.99x in the micro-benchmark, plus `toISO` and `toLocaleString`, which never call `Locale.create` (the interleaved micro-benchmark puts `toLocaleString` at 1.00x), and `toFormat with macro no cache`, which calls `Settings.resetCaches()` on every iteration and has margins of up to 14%. Creation and formatting paths that call `Locale.create` gain a few percent because the lookup is cheaper than constructing a `Locale`; paths that build Intl-derived name lists on a fresh `Locale` gain orders of magnitude because those lists are now computed once per configuration.

A differential run of 256,295 API calls (factories, formatting, parsing, `Info`, `Duration`, `Interval`, week math, `Settings` changes and `resetCaches` mid-run) produced identical output on master and this branch.

## Testing

`test/impl/locale.test.js` (new): same configuration shares one instance through `Locale.create` and through every `DateTime` factory and `Duration`; different configurations, including `weekSettings` by value and explicit-vs-fallback `en-US`, get distinct instances, and the fallback observably redefaults while the explicit one does not; each `Settings.default*` change yields a different instance and restoring the setting yields the original cached one; `Settings.resetCaches()` drops the cache; a cached `Locale` does not remember an Intl feature that was missing when it was created; `setLocale` / `reconfigure` output is unchanged for `fr`, `beng` digits and the Islamic calendar; `toFormat`'s redefault path hits the cache; sharing keeps working past the cache limits; deep-freezing one `DateTime` leaves others working.

`test/info/listers.test.js`: mutating an `Info` list no longer affects later calls, `DateTime` getters or parsing.

Existing suites pass unchanged.

## Open questions

- **Bounded or unbounded.** Luxon's other caches are unbounded. The bound here is cheap insurance against two new growth vectors that the Intl caches do not have: a `DateTime` created with a distinct locale string or `weekSettings` value now retains about 0.5 KB even if it is never formatted, and invalid locale strings are retained too (the Intl caches only store what `Intl` accepted). Each entry is small next to the ~35 KB of native ICU memory an `Intl.DateTimeFormat` costs once a locale is formatted, so dropping the bound to match convention is fine by me.
- **Opt-out.** Like the other caches this is always on. I did not add a setting to disable it, to avoid new API surface.
